resolutions.researcher_notes: Status 'operating' inferred from context: both sources report gas began flowing through the line (reversed direction, Israel→Egypt) in January 2020 and it is actively carrying gas — Al Jazeera 'Egypt started importing natural gas from Israel's Leviathan field on Wednesday'; World Oil 'Israeli gas finally reaches Egypt'. Two independent outlets. Line is currently operating.

Fuel=Gas: gulfoilandgas describes 'a submarine gas pipeline ... to transport approximately 7.0 BCM per annum of Egyptian natural gas'; INSS refers to it as a natural gas pipeline carrying 7-9 BCM. Two independent sources, both explicit natural gas.

StartYear1=2008 supported by gulfoilandgas milestones: 'Completion 2/25/2008' / 'The commissioning of the pipeline began' 2/25/2008 (original Egypt→Israel operation). StartYear2=2020 supported by Al Jazeera: Egypt began importing Israeli gas in January 2020 after the flow was reversed. Both start years independently sourced.

StopYear=2012: LA Times (23 Apr 2012) reports the Egypt-Israel gas deal was revoked in April 2012; Washington Institute states the flow 'was halted in 2012 following the election of a Muslim Brotherhood-led government and multiple terrorist attacks on the pipeline'. Two independent sources confirm the 2012 shutdown of the original Egypt→Israel flow.

Capacity=7.00 bcm/y: gulfoilandgas 'transport approximately 7.0 BCM per annum'; INSS notes upgrades 'have the potential capacity to increase the annual flow capacity, from 7 to 9 BCM' (i.e. baseline 7 BCM). Two independent sources agree on 7 bcm/y.

LengthKnown=90 km: INSS 'the 90 km pipeline from el-Arish to Ashkelon'; Offshore Technology 'the 90km EMG pipeline connects the Israeli and Egyptian pipeline networks'. Two independent sources agree on 90 km. CONTRADICTION FLAG: gulfoilandgas states '100 kilometres (62 mile)' for the same line — minority figure; the 90 km value has stronger corroboration and matches the GEM value.

FuelSource=Egypt supported for the ORIGINAL (2008-2012) design only: gulfoilandgas 'transport ... Egyptian natural gas to Israel'; Washington Institute 'originally built to supply Egyptian gas to Israel'. CONTRADICTION FLAG for review: since the 2020 reversal the physical fuel source is now ISRAEL (Tamar/Leviathan offshore fields → Egypt), per Al Jazeera and the OPIC/DFC project description (rightsindevelopment). The FuelSource=Egypt field reflects the pipeline's original configuration, not its current direction — flag for Update to decide whether it should reflect current (Israel) source.

Endpoints Ashkelon (Israel) ↔ El-Arish/Arish, North Sinai (Egypt): INSS 'the 90 km pipeline from el-Arish to Ashkelon'; OPIC/DFC project page (rightsindevelopment) 'a pipeline running from Al-Arish, Egypt, to Ashkelon, Israel'. Washington Institute separately places al-Arish in North Sinai. Two+ independent sources confirm both endpoints and countries.

Owner1=East Mediterranean Gas Co 61%, Owner2=EMED 39%: Offshore Technology 'Noble Energy and its partners have acquired a 39% equity interest in the Eastern Mediterranean Gas (EMG) company' (the EMED consortium = East Gas/Delek/Noble); INSS 'Delek Drilling ... purchased 39 percent of ... Eastern Mediterranean Gas (EMG)'. The remaining 61% stays with the original East Mediterranean Gas Company shareholders. Two independent sources confirm the 39% EMED stake and the complementary 61% split matching the GEM values.
